title: Safe and honest: preservatives, labels, NAFDAC, records

say: Safe and honest: preservatives, labels, NAFDAC and batch records.
This is the video for module 3 of Organic Skincare and Hair Products.
Bacteria, yeasts and moulds need water to multiply. In a lotion, they can grow into very large numbers within days in warm weather, often without anything you can see or smell.

panel.heading: Protect customers and your business
items: Water lets germs grow, often unseen
Your label and posts are promises
Batch records let you prove and repeat quality

say: In Nigeria, cosmetics are regulated by NAFDAC. Every word on your label and your WhatsApp posts is a promise.

say: And batch records let you prove your quality, and find the cause when something goes wrong.

say: An antioxidant, like vitamin E or rosemary extract, slows oils going rancid. It does not stop germs. Essential oils and grapefruit seed extract are not preservatives either.
A broad-spectrum preservative works against bacteria, yeasts and moulds. Any product containing water needs one.
Watch for hidden water: aloe vera, rose water, herbal teas and milk all bring water in.
Grace in Benin City sees a video of a natural whipped lotion: shea butter, aloe vera gel and vitamin E. She marks the hidden water. Aloe gel is mostly water.

panel.heading: Is this lotion safe to sell?
items: List ingredients; mark hidden water

Ask how long customers keep the jar
Decide; offer a water-free option

say: She looks for a broad-spectrum preservative. There is none. Vitamin E is only an antioxidant.

say: Lotions for sale need a tested preservative, the correct pH and laboratory testing. Until then, it is honest to say you make only water-free products.

panel.rule: Water and no named preservative? Do not make it for sale.

say: Once you claim to treat, cure or prevent a condition, you are making a medical claim that needs approval as a medicine. Never say cures, heals, guaranteed growth or lightens. Chemical-free is never true, and do not say certified organic without certification.
Say what you can prove. Joy in Owerri changed her post to: light scalp oil, testers with dry scalps found it light, not greasy. Patch test first.
And never add hydroquinone, mercury, steroid creams or crushed tablets. They cause serious harm.
Your label should show the product name, how to use it, the full ingredient list, the net content, and your name and address. Add the batch number, date made and best-before date.
Include warnings like patch test before use, contains nut oil, and keep out of reach of children. Check the current NAFDAC labelling rules before you print.

panel.heading: What your label should show
items: Product and brand name, how to use
Full ingredient list
Net content, maker's name and address
Batch number, made date, best-before
Warnings: patch test, nut oil, children
NAFDAC number, once registered

say: Registration starts with your business name at CAC, and your brand name with the Trademarks Registry.

say: Prepare your premises and keep good records from day one, because an inspection follows.

say: You apply online for each product, with label artwork and a laboratory certificate of analysis. Fees apply, and the guideline states 120 working days. Check current details on the NAFDAC website, because they change.

say: Give every batch a number, and write it on every jar. Ifeoma's customer said her hair oil smelled like old groundnut after two months. Ifeoma asked for the batch number.

say: Your best-before date can never be longer than your shortest-lived ingredient. Start modest, and check retained samples every month.

panel.rule: Keep one retained sample from every batch, cool and dark.

say: To remember. Anything with water needs a real preservative, and vitamin E is not one. Make only honest cosmetic claims. Put full, true information on your label.
And keep a batch number, a batch record and a retained sample for every run.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Water means a broad-spectrum preservative
Vitamin E and essential oils do not preserve
No cure, growth or lightening claims
Full, true label; check NAFDAC rules
Batch number, record and retained sample
